newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia port strike talks break up in disarray.
newsitem.headline: Colombia port strike talks break up in disarray.

text.p: Negotiations between dock workers, cargo operators and ship owners broke up early Thursday in apparent disarray and still without any deal to end the strike that has paralyzed Colombia's main Pacific coast port, a cargo operator said.

The marathon round of talks began Tuesday and lasted for 36 hours with just a few hours break early Wednesday. The strike at the port of Buenaventura is now in its ninth day and has blocked more than 300,000 60-kg bags of coffee exports and 27,000 tonnes of sugar exports.
The discussions are scheduled to resume at 1000 local time (1500 GMT) Thursday in the government buildings in provincial capital Cali, a local official, who had been sitting in on coversations, said.

"It's been a long session. There was quite a bit of bad feeling after deadlock began to set in, some of the ship owners and operators left furious," one cargo operator, who did not wish to be named, told Reuters in a phone interview.

Dock workers are demanding a deal that would boost cargo handling tariffs and almost double their wages, from the current average of about $80 per month. They also want guaranteed injury, sickness and social security benefits and additional meal allowances on the days they work.
The talks appear to have stalled, after early progress, on the issue of increased rates for handling sugar cargoes. All Colombia's sugar exports are shipped through Buenaventura.
It is estimated that the strike is costing the port of Buenaventura $500,000 for every day it continues, as well as paralyzing key exports.

Hopes emerged for an early end to the strike last Thursday but dockers rejected an agreement in principle which their representatives had hammered out with the other parties in the dispute. (--Karl Penhaul, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944)
